#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -t 24:00:00
#   -J pico
#   --mail-user=simpson@ukp.informatik.tu-darmstadt.de
#   --mail-type=FAIL
#   -e ./pico.err.%j
#   -o ./pico.out.%j
#   -n 1
#   -c 16
#   --mem-per-cpu=8182
#   --exclusive
#   -C avx

#flux: --job-name=pico
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 16
#flux: --time-limit=24h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=8182
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --exclusive
# Flux exclusivity is site/config dependent; no universally portable batch directive.
# Performance implication: job may share a node with other jobs, causing contention and reduced performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: -C avx (CPU feature constraint)
# Flux constraints/feature selection are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may land on nodes lacking AVX, potentially causing illegal-instruction failures or reduced performance.

# Omitted Slurm options: --mail-user / --mail-type
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic failure emails.

# Omitted Slurm options: -o/-e with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

module load intel python/3.6.8
python -u ./src/run_pico_experiments.py

reasons: The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu=8182`), but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
The original Slurm job requested exclusive node access (`--exclusive`), but the Flux resource section has no exclusivity request; node sharing can introduce contention and performance variability.
The original Slurm job constrained CPU features (`-C avx`), but the Flux resource section has no feature constraint; the job could be placed on nodes without AVX, risking failure or slower execution.
